voice.name: Alice - Clear, Engaging Educator
voice.note: clear middle-aged British female — a physician recounting her own documented case

segments.c_open: I strung threads across the staircase. Thin ones, in the dark, where nobody could see them. [pause] She came down through them. Not one was broken.
segments.c_s1: June, eighteen eighty-two. I was nineteen, and I was studying medicine — which is to say I was being trained to observe a thing carefully and write it down. [pause] Somebody was at my door. I opened it: nobody. A few steps along the passage, and there she was, at the head of the stairs. A tall lady, in black. I followed her down. My candle-end burnt itself out, and I lost her in the dark.
segments.c_s2: Black — a soft woollen material; you could hear it move. Widow's weeds, cuffs at both wrists. And the face hidden, in a handkerchief, held in the right hand. [pause] Always the right hand. She was not transparent. She was not a mist. Seventeen people saw her, over four years, and most took her for a living woman in the house.
segments.c_s3: I spoke to her. The twenty-ninth of January, eighteen eighty-four — I asked her if I could help her. [pause] I got a slight gasp. Nothing more. I tried to touch her; my hand met nothing, and she was past me. I cornered her once, in a room with one door. She simply was not there any more. So I stopped chasing, and I started measuring. Threads. Across the stairs, at intervals. She passed. Nothing broke.
segments.c_s4: I wrote it all down as it happened — dates, times, who was in the house, what each of them saw. Then I sent it to the Society for Psychical Research, and they printed it. [pause] The gentleman who edited it called it one of the best authenticated instances of haunting on record. He also described me, in print, as a lady of scientific training. He meant it kindly. It was also a defence.
segments.c_s5: She came less often after eighty-seven, and after eighty-nine, not at all. [pause] I qualified. I was the twenty-third woman in England to take a medical degree, and I spent my working life as a physician — some of it inside a women's prison, where nobody has time for ghosts. I never claimed to know what she was. I claimed what I saw, and what I did to test it. [pause] The threads were not broken. Make of that what you will.

small: The witness is a medical student.

yt_title: Cheltenham: She Walked Through My Threads
